title: The Engineer's Guide to Meaningful Commit Messages: Beyond git log Noise
excerpt: Clear commit history is maintainable code's first line of defense.

content.text: Every project I've worked on has taught me one constant: a git log filled with 'fix typos' or 'wip' entries becomes a liability, not a history.
Why Commit Messages Matter More Than We Admit
When a team of five pushes daily without conventions, debugging production incidents turns into archaeological dig. You find yourself grepping for 'maybe fix this' or 'attempt 2' across branches.
If you have to explain what the code does in a commit message, the code probably needs refactoring.
content.author: Kent Beck

content.text: In a Flutter + FastAPI workflow, where state changes ripple across platforms, a well-structured commit becomes the single source of truth for what changed and why.

I've settled on a simple format: type(scope): short summary, followed by a blank line and a wrapped description. Types like feat, fix, docs, refactor, test keep the log scannable. For mobile work, I often add platform tags like (flutter|web|supabase) in the scope.

Automation helps. A simple Husky pre-commit hook or GitHub Actions check that validates the pattern reduces friction. The goal isn't enforcement for its own sake — it's making the git log a useful debugging tool, not a chore.
A git history worth reading is a git history worth writing.
content.author: Unknown

content.text: If you're tired of hunting through noise to find why a feature broke, start with the commit. The discipline pays off far beyond the terminal.
